objective:
Discover new mechanisms in which TRAINING-ONLY user behaviour and HYPERBOLIC geometry are computationally coupled to improve the RQ-VAE Semantic IDs used by a generative next-item recommender, with the real target of Stage3 test Recall@10 above 0.065.

## The measured lever, and the mechanism of the one family that reaches 0.0636

Nine mechanisms on the frozen baseline (Stage 2: 3000 epochs, four cards; Stage 3: 150
epochs, width-20 beam, 57,439 rows) all land at or below the baseline's own 0.055537,
including one that reached the structural profile the forensics asked for (16 behaviour
cohorts, positive-prefix rate 0.49, depth-1 survival 1.000, depth-2 0.656).

Reading the Stage 2 tree of the one family whose SID reaches 0.0636 identifies the
difference: it applies a **temperature-scaled contrastive loss to the three residual
vectors themselves** (sources are the batch's items, candidates their mined train-only
successors, the metric is the Euclidean residual distance, and the weight ramps linearly to
0.20). This round implements exactly that mechanism on the frozen baseline.

## What the mechanism must do

* mine the (source, successor) pairs from training histories only;
* take the three pre-quantisation residuals of one forward (differentiable in the encoder
  and the first two codebooks), and the residuals of the mined successors;
* apply a contrastive cross-entropy with the Euclidean residual distance divided by a
  temperature, one term per level, averaged;
* ramp the weight linearly from zero so the codebook forms before the contrast acts;
* behaviour-off shuffles the successors of every pair, geometry-off replaces the residual
  distance with the distance in the *raw encoder output* (the same pairs and weights).

Scale discipline matters and was learned the hard way: the term at full weight is O(1)
against a reconstruction loss of ~1e-4, so the ramp and the averaging over levels are what
keep it stable. An implementation that adds a second forward over the whole batch, or that
applies the contrast to the assigned codewords, collapses the assignment (measured: 1-4
distinct SIDs out of 24,587).

## Required measurement contract

State the predicted direction of `L1 Hard ER` (canonical 52,855 pairs, ten fixed
negatives), gold-prefix survival at depths 1-4, teacher-forced top-1 accuracy of T1..T4
(with the extension-token alphabet in particular), and Stage 3 `test_R@10`. The reference is
0.055537 (the baseline control) and the target is 0.065.

## Frozen constraints

Four tokens, 3000 Stage 2 epochs on four cards, no early stopping, no test-time tuning, the
frozen Stage 3 protocol, no validation or test behaviour in SID construction, and a
one-epoch smoke that must stay numerically stable.

findings.correction: Make the artanh bound representably below 1 in the input dtype (for example `1 - torch.finfo(x.dtype).eps`, or clamp in float64 with a defined cast policy) and add a finite guard. Pass `geometry_on=GEOMETRY_ON` explicitly at the call site (or resolve the setting at call time). Validate finite loss and encoder gradients and compare both-on, behaviour-off, and Euclidean runs in the prescribed smoke.
findings.detail: The float32 `artanh` clamp uses `1 - 1e-10`; in float32 this rounds to exactly 1. If `sqrt(c)*norm` reaches or rounds to 1, `log1p(-x)` becomes negative infinity and Poincare distance/loss/gradients can become non-finite. This violates the required numerical stability for the actual float32 contrast path. In addition, trainer's `GEOMETRY_ON` setting is not passed to `_residual_contrast` (whose default is captured at definition), so toggling the trainer constant off does not select the Euclidean branch; this prevents the specified trainer-level geometry-off comparison.
findings.reproduction: Minimal counterexample: evaluate `artanh(torch.tensor([1.0], dtype=torch.float32))`; the clamp maximum rounds to 1.0 and the result is infinite. Separately set `GEOMETRY_ON = False` before `main()` and observe that calls at train_rqvae.py:421 still use the default `geometry_on=True`.
